TL;DR


## Key takeaways


1. Coinflow is acceptance infrastructure that settles card payments into USDC in minutes, with payouts back to fiat.
2. Infinite operates the account layer beneath acceptance, where each customer holds an individually titled demand deposit account.
3. The same Infinite Account sends and receives SWIFT wires and moves dollars over ACH, Fedwire, and RTP.
4. On Infinite, third-party flows are the design center, with every customer onboarded, screened, and monitored across the whole program.
5. First-time reviews that traditionally take around 30 days close in one to two days on Infinite.


01


## Acceptance in, accounts underneath


Coinflow has built real acceptance machinery: card payments that settle into USDC in minutes rather than days, indemnified chargeback protection, marketplace split payments, and SDKs across major platforms. For merchants and marketplaces that want fiat acceptance with stablecoin settlement, it is a credible, fast-moving option.


Infinite operates a different layer. The question it answers is not "how do I get paid" but "what do my customers hold, and who answers for the money moving":[a real demand deposit account per customer](https://infinite.net/accounts/managed) at chartered, FDIC-insured bank partners, with the rails and the compliance program built into the account.


02


## What your customer holds


On acceptance platforms, settled funds typically land in a hosted balance or an on-chain wallet. On Infinite, every customer holds an individually titled DDA with its own account and routing numbers,[not a sub-ledger on a pooled account](https://infinite.net/resources/learn/glossary/virtual-account) , with USDC, USDT, OUSD, and USDG beside fiat, converting by native mint and burn with no intermediary liquidity providers. For businesses that will not touch self-custody, the[Wallet Account](https://infinite.net/accounts/wallets) keeps stablecoin custody inside a chartered bank partner's perimeter: the customer holds the balance, the bank holds the wallet and its keys.


> Getting paid is an event. Holding and moving money is an operation, and the operation is what regulators examine.


03


## Rails from the account, not around it


The same Infinite Account[sends and receives SWIFT wires](https://infinite.net/payments/swift) (Coinflow's public docs describe wire support as US-domestic), moves dollars over ACH, Fedwire, and RTP, and runs FX across GBP, EUR, MXN, and BRL at firm, all-in quotes, with additional corridors including AED and INR being added. Stablecoin transfers settle in minutes, 24/7, and SWIFT wires run from the same account.


04


## Built for third-party flows


Acceptance platforms generally serve merchants directly, under merchant terms. The harder problem arrives when your platform moves money that belongs to your customers; then regulators expect customer-level diligence on every one of them. On Infinite,[third-party flows are the design center](https://infinite.net/resources/funds-flow/third-party) : each customer onboards through[whitelabel flows in your brand](https://infinite.net/agents/embedded-compliance) , gets a real account, and is screened and monitored across your whole program, with AI assembling each case file inside[human-approved policy and judgment calls routed to named analysts](https://infinite.net/agents/compliance-agent) . First-time reviews that traditionally take around 30 days close in 1–2, and a counterparty vetted once is vetted for every business on the network.


05


## When Coinflow fits


If the job is accepting card and crypto payments with instant stablecoin settlement (a game, a marketplace, an e-commerce checkout), Coinflow is built for that moment, and the two products can sit in the same stack. If the job is what happens after acceptance (customers holding balances in their own accounts, payouts over SWIFT and local rails, an operated compliance program underneath),[that is the job Infinite is built for](https://infinite.net/resources/funds-flow/third-party) .


FAQ


## Frequently asked questions


### Does Infinite do payment acceptance or checkout?


No, Infinite is not a card acquirer. Businesses typically accept payments through a processor and use Infinite as the layer underneath: real accounts where customers hold fiat and stablecoin balances, rails for moving funds globally, and the compliance program governing it all. The two layers pair naturally.


### Can customers hold stablecoins in their own account on Infinite?


Yes. Each customer's account holds USDC, USDT, OUSD, and USDG beside fiat. For custody, bank-owned wallets are established and controlled by a chartered bank partner: your customer holds the balance, the bank holds the wallet and its keys, and your team never touches key management.


### Does Infinite work for marketplaces?


Yes. Marketplaces move money that belongs to sellers, which makes them third-party flows: every seller gets a real account, onboarded in your brand, with screening and portfolio-wide monitoring run by the network and documented for auditors.
